question: What should we measure first to reduce latency for two concurrent Qwen3-8B v5 research readers on the previously used 24 GB A5000 setup?

task.value: Bounded multi-step paper research with Python document-tool actions executed in network-disabled Docker.

hardware.value: Historical RTX A5000, 25285623808 reported bytes; no current hardware activated or attested.

workload.value: Fixed-input serving diagnostic: historical_reader_request_2 (1400 recomputed input tokens) and historical_reader_request_6 (2043); exact saved payload hashes in profile-input-manifest.json. Not full reader episodes or an answer-quality benchmark.

constraints: This walkthrough permits public source retrieval and local records only: zero new Qwen/Nemotron calls or GPU provisioning.
Preserve checkpoints, decoding and prompt/corpus identity for any future controlled test.
Two readers are a target; historical configured max sequences is not a concurrent load measurement.

observations.text: Historical startup reported 15.31 GiB weights, 4.39 GiB KV cache, 31952 cache-token slots, context limit 8192 and max sequences 2. These are startup/serial observations only.
The historical reader returned incomplete with no evidence; no two-reader, TTFT, prefill or decode baseline is available in this selected export.

alternatives: First localize serving/queue overhead with fixed inputs.
Consider prefix caching only if reusable prefill is material; verify actual runtime support/configuration.
Consider decode methods only after identifying decode cost; do not infer benefit from paper speedups.
proposed_change: Dispatch the same pinned pair of historical reader inputs concurrently rather than serially on one unchanged serving engine. First validate instrumentation, same-engine overlap and cache-state control.
hypothesis: Concurrent dispatch may reduce pair completion time if the serving path admits overlapping inference; scheduler serialization, KV pressure or additional waiting can erase the benefit. No speedup is assumed.
expected_signal: Two counterbalanced measured rounds expose pair makespan, all eight measured completions, actual token counts, engine overlap, phase timing and memory. A serialized route or missing phase telemetry identifies an instrumentation/transport prerequisite instead of a model optimization win.
applicability: A tiny warm fixed-input serving diagnostic for the previously used Qwen3-8B/v5 setup. It does not estimate two complete agents, long-output performance, supported-answer quality, changes in response to new feedback, or the benefit of MCP over ordinary research.

procedure: Preflight only after separate authorization: verify payload hashes, current weights/adapter/runtime, one engine, admission overlap, matching tokenizer, engine metrics access, cache-state control and a durable request/token/lifecycle budget. Stop before paid dispatch if a prerequisite is missing.

Use two unmeasured warmup requests (one per payload). Reset or otherwise equalize the declared cache state per measured batch while keeping the engine loaded; include any extra generation warmups in the same request cap or stop.
Round 1: run the pair serially, then concurrently. Round 2: concurrently, then serially. Preserve failed/missing cases and per-request timestamps; 8 measured plus 2 warmup requests total.

Capture pair makespan and each request completion latency at the client, actual input/output token counts and finish reasons; collect engine queue/prefill/decode timing, same-engine concurrency, KV usage/preemptions and GPU memory separately. Provider delay/execution time is not a substitute for engine phases.

Stop at 10 total model requests, 7168 input/1024 output reservation each (81920 tokens total), or on identity mismatch, missing telemetry, OOM, timeout or uncertain submission; never resubmit an uncertain inference. Future compute duration/spending limits still require approval and lifecycle enforcement.

Treat any apparent latency change as inconclusive if output lengths/finish reasons or cache state differ materially. Two measured rounds are diagnostic only: no p95/p99, useful-answer or general speedup claim. Do not record results until an actual authorized run exists.
